answer: A submission must carry a Merkle proof against the checkpoint sealed 16 blocks earlier, and the proof is verified before the text is even read. Since the thread verifier rejects a stale root immediately, the operator pays a fresh proof per key, and the beacon audit keeps every accepted path. A farm cannot batch-generate those proofs offline, because the checkpoint moves every epoch and each alias needs its own hollow path. That is 40 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
